translations.zh: 朝錯為太子家令，得幸皇太子，數從容言吳過可削。
translations.literal: Chao Cuo served as tutor to the crown prince's household. Favored by the crown prince, he repeatedly spoke privately that Wu's offenses could be grounds for reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo served as tutor to the crown prince's household. Favored by the crown prince, he repeatedly spoke privately that Wu's offenses could be grounds for reduction.

translations.zh: 數上書說之，文帝寬，不忍罰，以此吳王日益橫。
translations.literal: He submitted memorials urging this repeatedly. Emperor Wen was lenient and unwilling to punish; because of this the King of Wu grew more arrogant by the day.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials urging this repeatedly. Emperor Wen was lenient and unwilling to punish; because of this the King of Wu grew more arrogant by the day.

translations.zh: 及景帝即位，錯為御史大夫，說上曰：「昔高帝初定天下，昆弟少，諸子弱，大封同姓，故孽子悼惠王王齊七十二城，庶弟元王王楚四十城，兄子王吳五十餘城。
translations.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, Cuo became Grandee Secretary. He urged the emperor, "When Gaozu first settled the realm, his brothers were few and his sons were young. He enfeoffed many of the same surname. Thus the illegitimate son King Dao Hui ruled Qi with seventy-two cities; the younger brother King Yuan ruled Chu with forty cities; and his brother's son ruled Wu with more than fifty cities.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing took the throne, Cuo became Grandee Secretary. He urged the emperor, "When Gaozu first settled the realm, his brothers were few and his sons were young. He enfeoffed many of the same surname. Thus the illegitimate son King Dao Hui ruled Qi with seventy-two cities; the younger brother King Yuan ruled Chu with forty cities; and his brother's son ruled Wu with more than fifty cities.

translations.literal: Three illegitimate branches held half the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Three illegitimate branches held half the realm.

translations.zh: 今吳王前有太子之隙，詐稱病不朝，於古法當誅。
translations.literal: Now the King of Wu, having earlier had a falling-out over the crown prince, feigned illness and failed to attend court—in ancient law this was punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: Now the King of Wu, having earlier had a falling-out over the crown prince, feigned illness and failed to attend court—in ancient law this was punishable by death.

translations.zh: 文帝不忍，因賜几杖，德至厚也。
translations.literal: Emperor Wen could not bear it and therefore granted him an armrest and staff—a kindness of the utmost depth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen could not bear it and therefore granted him an armrest and staff—a kindness of the utmost depth.

translations.zh: 不改過自新，乃益驕恣，公即山鑄錢，煮海為鹽，誘天下亡人謀作亂逆。
translations.literal: Rather than reform and renew himself, he grew all the more arrogant and overbearing: he openly minted coin at the mountains and boiled sea water for salt, enticing fugitives throughout the realm to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than reform and renew himself, he grew all the more arrogant and overbearing: he openly minted coin at the mountains and boiled sea water for salt, enticing fugitives throughout the realm to plot rebellion.

translations.literal: If we reduce him now, he will rebel; if we do not reduce him, he will rebel too.
translations.idiomatic: If we reduce him now, he will rebel; if we do not reduce him, he will rebel too.

translations.literal: If we reduce him, his rebellion will come quickly and the calamity will be small;
translations.idiomatic: If we reduce him, his rebellion will come quickly and the calamity will be small;

translations.literal: if we do not reduce him, his rebellion will come late and the calamity will be great."
translations.idiomatic: if we do not reduce him, his rebellion will come late and the calamity will be great."

translations.zh: 三年冬，楚王來朝，錯因言楚王戊往年為薄太后服，私姦服舍，請誅之。
translations.literal: In the third year, winter, the King of Chu came to court. Cuo therefore reported that the King of Chu, Wu, in earlier years while in mourning for Empress Dowager Bo, had had illicit relations in the mourning quarters, and asked that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, winter, the King of Chu came to court. Cuo therefore reported that the King of Chu, Wu, in earlier years while in mourning for Empress Dowager Bo, had had illicit relations in the mourning quarters, and asked that he be executed.

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him but stripped the Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him but stripped the Donghai commandery.

translations.zh: 及前二年，趙王有罪，削其常山郡。
translations.literal: In the year before last, the King of Zhao was found guilty and his Changshan commandery was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the year before last, the King of Zhao was found guilty and his Changshan commandery was stripped.

translations.zh: 膠西王卬以賣爵事有姦，削其六縣。
translations.literal: The King of Jiaoxi, Ang, had improprieties in the sale of noble ranks; six counties were stripped from him.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Jiaoxi, Ang, had improprieties in the sale of noble ranks; six counties were stripped from him.
